newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NATO position "unjust and wrong" - Yeltsin aide.
newsitem.headline: NATO position "unjust and wrong" - Yeltsin aide.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's foreign policy adviser on Tuesday denounced NATO's refusal to grant Russia a veto right on key isssues after its planned expansion eastwards as "strange, unjust and wrong", Interfax news agency said.
Dmitry Ryurikov, stepping up Moscow's war of words against NATO's plans to incorporate some former Warsaw Pact states, said the expansion posed a direct military threat to Russia.

NATO has vowed to expand regardless of Russian misgivings but has offered Moscow "special relations" as compensation. Russia says this is not enough and wants a "binding agreement" that would effectively give it a right of veto.

"It is an extremely strange position," Interfax quoted Ryurikov. He referred to "opinions expressed in the West over the impermissibility of granting Russia a veto right over issues concerning the safety of the continent."
"It is unjust and wrong," he said.
Ryurikov said there was a consensus in Russia over NATO's expansion plans and added this was a result of the "purely military threat" that it would imply.
